title: Compatibility Gatekeeper: onboarding spec & stability gates for pinned model versions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define and implement a Compatibility Gatekeeper that enforces backward-compatibility contracts for pinned model versions during onboarding and releases. This ticket specifies the acceptance criteria, validation tests, performance-profile publishing format, and rollout gating for models that customers can pin. The Gatekeeper should be a test-and-publish pipeline run as part of model onboarding and every pinned-model candidate release.

Scope and responsibilities:
- Contract areas covered: prompt format shape, structured/semantic output schema, stable inference parameters (e.g., temperature, max_tokens, top_p ranges), model artifact compatibility (KV cache layout/backward-compatible checkpoints), and published performance metrics (latency/throughput/memory).
- Validation: syntactic schema checks + semantic invariants + performance regression tests.
- Publishing: create a human- and machine-readable performance_profile JSON artifact stored in the model registry and surfaced in the Console.
- Gate behavior: onboarding fails if any stability gate is violated; partial passes allowed with documented opt-ins (see 'Allowed relaxations').

Acceptance criteria (must be automated):
1) Prompt/output shape invariants: Provide a schema bundle (OpenAPI/JSON Schema) per pinned model version. The gate runs a suite of 150+ template-driven prompts (edge cases, truncation, function-calling shapes) and verifies output conforms to the schema. Failures must be categorized as "hard" (breaks consumer contract) or "soft" (format variance). Hard failures block.
2) Semantic regression harness: Run embedding-similarity and token-level diff tests against a baseline pinned version. Thresholds: mean embedding cosine >= 0.92 across reference set OR task-specific quality metric drop <= 2%. Any regression flagged must include example cases and a reproducible script.
3) Performance profile publishing: Produce a performance_profile JSON with fields: model_id, version, hw_target, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, mean_throughput_tps, peak_memory_mb, kv_cache_compatibility (boolean), test_dataset_tag, test_seed, test_date, test_env_hash, and perf_signatures (list of representative scenario names). Profile hosted at: s3://redwood-model-profiles/<model_id>/<version>/performance_profile.json and linked in the model registry.
4) Latency/throughput gates: p95 increase vs baseline <= 10% (absolute tolerance 50ms). Mean throughput drop <= 15%. Memory increase <= 20% absolute. Exemptions require documented mitigation and PM approval.
5) Parameter surface stability: Allowed changes must be additive and documented. Examples: introducing new optional kwargs is OK; changing default max_tokens is a breaking change unless backward compatibility shim exists. Gate enforces a declared allowed_changes.json per model version.
6) KV cache and state compatibility: Verify run-to-run resumability on a set of sequence continuation tests. If incompatible, flag and require migration plan.
7) Release metadata: The Gatekeeper attaches a "compatibility_badge" with values ["compatible","compatible-with-warnings","incompatible"] and an automated summary table for Console and release notes.

Test harness and tooling:
- Add a new repository folder: tools/compat-gate/ with orchestrator, schema validator, semantic harness, and perf runner. Initial implementation uses existing load-test infra (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4862) and the perf dashboard endpoint (https://dashboard.redwood.ai/perf/onboarding/ENG-24177).
- Conformance tests are seeded from a centrally maintained prompt corpus: s3://redwood-test-corpora/compatibility/2026-02.
- Gate runs in CI for PRs that touch model manifests, and as a nightly job for all pinned versions.

Operational considerations and rollout policy:
- Canary: New gate enabled in "monitor" mode for 2 weeks (records failures but does not block) for initial set of 10 pinned models. After stabilization, flip to blocking for 30-day staged rollout by customer tier.
- Deprecation window: Breaking contract changes must carry a 90-day deprecation notice for enterprise customers; the Gatekeeper will annotate the registry and Console.
- Alerts: Failures above 3 per day trigger an incident to "inference-pulse" channel; perf regressions trigger a severity-2 review.

Deliverables:
- Compatibility Gatekeeper service + CI integration in tools/compat-gate (initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/212).
- Performance profile JSON schema and registry upload hook (spec and tests under docs/perf-profile-spec.md).
- Console UI change to surface compatibility_badge and per-version failure summaries (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Compatibility+Gatekeeper+UI).
- Migration playbook for model owners and a template "allowed_changes.json" to declare opt-ins.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Strict vs permissive gating: aggressive gating reduces production regressions but increases on-boarding friction for model partners. Proposal: Start permissive (monitoring) for community models, strict for enterprise pinned versions.
- Semantic metrics: single global threshold may not fit task-specific models (e.g., summarization vs code). We propose per-project override hooks in the model manifest.
- Test flakiness: invest in deterministic seeds and environment hashing to reduce noise.

Next steps (short-term):
- Prototype schema validator and publish perf profile schema (owner: Liam O'Connor).
- Wire basic CI run for one internal pinned model and collect initial metrics (owner: Maya Chen).
- PM and Design sign-off on Console surfacing (scheduled review 2026-03-18).

Notes: See related artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Compatibility+Gatekeeper+PRD, perf test harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4862, onboarding dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/perf/onboarding/ENG-24177.
